fixes.explanation: Paul actually says the opposite of that. He says, "For he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law." So loving your neighbor isn't a side note to the law. It's the law fulfilled, friend.

That's the one! Paul says the commandments, and any other commandments, are summed up in one decree, and the decree is "Love your neighbor as yourself." (Romans 13:9) That's a whole list squeezed into one sentence. I can't even fit my grocery list on one sticky note, friend.

Paul says it straight: "Love does no wrong to its neighbor." Then he adds, "Therefore love is the fulfillment of the law." Love isn't out there looking for ways to hurt anybody. Meanwhile my mustache knocks over a cookie box every other week.

Passover is a real feast (Exodus 12:14), but Paul isn't talking about it in this passage. What he says is, "…our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed." That's the thing getting closer, and it's why he wants them awake.

That's right. Paul says to behave decently, "…not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in dissension and jealousy." So dissension and jealousy sit right on the same list. They're named right alongside the rest, friend.

That's the one! Paul says, "Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ…" He puts it right after the list of things to leave behind. Not the prophets, not the angels, but the Lord Jesus Christ Himself, friend.
